question: Does the exact P65 AP expose a usable stock NuttX module-loader path for Canopus?
control_flow_evidence: The active IDA database input is the exact P65 AP: SHA-256 a19b601477569765103eaf468b937bd8026b4d68ffa5c896bde222a79e475858, size 11,793,540 bytes, entry 0x0C0C0010.

The NSH command string pool near `nsh_command.c` (0x0C2844F0) includes alphabetized built-in help names: `insmod` at 0x0C2848C0 with usage `<file-path> <module-name>` at 0x0C2848C8, `lsmod` at 0x0C284988, and `rmmod` at 0x0C284B90; ordinary shell commands are adjacent.

The XIP strings also include module/mod_insmod.c (0x0C2591FC), module/mod_rmmod.c (0x0C259210), module/mod_modhandle.c (0x0C259224), module/mod_procfs.c (0x0C25923C), modlib/modlib_load.c (0x0C27017C), modlib/modlib_loadhdrs.c (0x0C270194), modlib/modlib_registry.c (0x0C2701B0), modlib/modlib_symtab.c (0x0C2701CC), and binfmt_execmodule.c/binfmt_execsymtab.c near 0x0C3A403D.

IDA records zero data xrefs to the tested command/source-string addresses. Full-width XIP, cached, non-cached, bare file-offset, and tested 0x3C raw-flash-alias pointer searches found no encoding for the command/help strings; a scan of 1,890 ADR instructions found no target within 0x80 of the four command-name/usage strings. The XIP inventory has 46,916 strings but only 13 with recorded xrefs, so these negatives are an analysis-coverage limitation, not proof that components are inactive.
The nearby generic `module` error strings at 0x0C287A44-0x0C287B78 belong to Lua 5.4 (`package.searchers`, `luaopen_%s`, `LUA_CPATH`), not evidence of NuttX `modlib` behavior.

Follow-up exact-AP analysis recovered the NSH insmod/rmmod handlers, ELF load/bind path, ARM relocation switch, module-list insertion/removal, and symbol-resolution sources; see EVID-P65-MODLIB-001. Later startup disassembly reconstructed the 0x3C data/BSS VMA and boot values; see EVID-P65-MEMORY-002. Canopus compatibility remains unverified.
unsafe_assumptions: A source-path or command-help string is not proof that its implementation is linked, registered, reachable, or compatible with Canopus; similarly, Lua dynamic-module messages are not evidence of NuttX ELF-loader behavior.

P65 IDA data-reference coverage is sparse and the current IDA database still does not map the runtime 0x3C VMA directly. EVID-P65-MEMORY-002 reconstructs command/data contents through the startup copy/zero path, but physical memory type and post-startup writes remain unresolved.

Relocation cases and static lifecycle code are recovered, but runtime relocation behavior, symbol-table population, exact name/path validation, constructor ordering, failure/concurrency ownership, autoload behavior, Canopus compatibility and physical-device safety remain unverified.
recommended_probe: Determine whether the zero-count static symbol table is populated after startup, audit Canopus Manager imports against available dynamic exports, and reconcile the recovered initializer/unload ABI with a target-specific shim. Keep P65 non-deployable until a reviewed no-op test module and recovery plan are device-validated.
